title: Popular items stripped from shelves in mass recalls across Australia - Yahoo Lifestyle Australia
text:
Product recall roundup: Pump water bottles, Aldi TV stand, garden item sold at Mitre 10 - Yahoo Lifestyle Australia Search query for Search the web Search the web Skip to main 
 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to homepage Product recall roundup: Pump water bottles, Aldi TV stand, garden item sold at Mitre 10
 Several items, including a popular bottled water, have been pulled from shelves this week.
 Claudia Poposki Sat 7 November 2026 at 6:00 pm UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. There has been an array of potentially dangerous products recalled this week that could be in your fridge, living room, or backyard.
 Consumer safety watchdogs and companies are constantly on the lookout for items that don't meet safety standards or pose a risk to human health.
 Yahoo Lifestyle has done a wrap-up of the items to be aware of.
 Items sold in supermarkets across the country have been pulled over fears they pose a risk to human safety.
 (Getty) Pump water pulled from shelves due to a packaging fault
 Coca-Cola Australia recalled five versions of Pump due to the risk of the white sipper dislodging, creating a choking hazard.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The bottles were sold at Woolworths, Coles, Aldi, independent food retailers including IGA, petrol stations, convenience stores, newsagents, vending machines, and retail outlets nationally and online
 "Consumers should not drink this product," the recall said.
 These Pump water bottles have been recalled across Australia.
 (FSANZ/Getty) The products recalled include:
 1.25L Super Pump Spring Water - all Best Before dates up to and including 22 January 2028
 750mL Pump Spring Water - all Best Before dates up to and including 22 January 2028
 750mL Pump Watermelon Hit - all Best Before dates up to and including 23 April 2027
 750mL Pump Lime Ruse - all Best Before dates up to and including 23 April 2027
 750mL Pump Berry Storm - all Best Before dates up to and including 23 April 2027
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement If you have questions or need more information about the recall, you can contact Coca-Cola.
 The company has a hotline at +61 2 8249 9113 and an email address at consumer_information@ccep.com . 
 Aldi TV stand recalled over warning label issue
 Aldi issued an alert on Thursday about its SOHL TV Floor Stand, which was sold nationally between August and October.
 The stand didn't have warning labels about toppling furniture, and "consumers may not be aware of the hazards".
 If users are unaware and it's not properly secured, there is a "risk of serious injury or death", according to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.

 Love Island Australia's Shawnee Schein dumped from brand deal after 'inappropriate' comments 
 Baby Boomer's controversial demand at Aussie cafe sparks fierce debate 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement No cases of this have happened.
 The impacted products are barcodes that read 4069365483145 or 4069365194034.
 People can also check Stock Keeping Units to see if their floor stand was recalled; the units are 718407 and 718408.
 There is a hotline open from Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5:30pm, which is 13 25 34.
 You can also email the supermarket on customer@service.aldi.com.au or visit their website .
 The TV stand was available for sale nationwide for eight weeks.
 (ACCC/Getty) Garden item sold at Mitre 10 and discount stores
 Yatsal Distributors recalled a version of its Pro Garden LED Solar Lamp because it didn't comply with mandatory standards for products containing button batteries.
 The ACCC said the product was not tested prior to sale and is missing warning information about the dangers surrounding the type of battery and what to do when someone swallows one.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Children are at risk of choking, serious injury or death if they swallow or place button batteries inside their bodies," the consumer watchdog said.
 These garden lamps have been recalled for not having crucial information about button batteries.
 (ACCC) "Stop using the product immediately and keep out of reach of children. Return the product to the place of purchase for a full refund."
 The issue affected the company's tulip version of the lamp, which comes in four colours, and is only for those with the batch code of 6195.
 It was sold between early August and mid-October, and was available at a range of discount and hardware stores, including two Mitre 10 locations.
 You can contact Yatsal Distributors on 02 9755 8735 between 9am and 4:30pm AEST, Monday to Friday or email compliance@yatsal.com.au .
